draft.article:
Voters across Miami-Dade and Broward counties will decide whether to extend a property tax that boosts teacher salaries and funds school safety measures.

First implemented in 2018, the special tax must be renewed every four years. During the 2022 election, the measure passed with 65 percent of the vote in Miami-Dade and 57 percent in Broward.

Broward Teachers Union President Anna Fusco emphasized that the supplemental funds are vital to help educators stay in local classrooms without needing second or third jobs driving ride-shares or delivering food.

The renewal proposal currently holds widespread bipartisan backing from both Democrats and Republicans throughout South Florida.

items.title: What Would Happen If Sea Level Rose 10 Feet In Florida

headlines: A TEN FOOT SEA LEVEL RISE WOULD SUBMERGE LOW MIAMI BEACH STREETS
TEN FEET HIGHER: WHAT HAPPENS TO MIAMI BEACH
CAN MIAMI DEFENSES SURVIVE TEN FEET OF RISING OCEAN WATER
draft.article: A hypothetical ten-foot rise in ocean levels would put low streets across Miami Beach beneath everyday tides. Situated between the Atlantic Ocean and Biscayne Bay, low-lying ground would stay underwater without massive defensive upgrades. Seawalls alone cannot prevent flooding because South Florida rests on porous limestone, which lets rising groundwater bubble up from underneath. This rising water table compromises septic systems that require dry soil to process waste. Miami-Dade is already converting vulnerable septic tanks to sewer lines in Little River, working to protect communities and the Biscayne aquifer that provides our drinking water.

draft.article:
Miami-Dade County has broken its all-time annual record for ultra-luxury residential sales in just the first nine months of 2026. Buyers closed on 24 single-family houses and condominiums priced at $30 million or higher through September, surpassing the previous full-year record of 21 transactions set in 2025.

Market tracking by MIAMI REALTORS and RWorld indicates the county could reach 32 mega-deals by year end. While wealthy purchasers fueled record high-end activity, overall county residential sales dropped two percent in September to 1,733 closings as borrowing costs climbed, with mortgage rates reaching 7.46 percent in October. Still, local single-family median prices rose over four percent to $692,000.
